author_zh: 後秦 釋僧肇 撰
author_en: Venerable Sengzhao, disciple of Kumārajīva (Eastern Jin / Later Qin)
era: Later Qin Dynasty, early 5th century CE (404–414 CE)
genre: Mādhyamika treatise (中觀四論), foundational Sinitic Buddhist philosophy cited by Chan masters
overview: Sengzhao's Zhao Lun (肇論) — four treatises (On the Immutability of Things, On the Emptiness of the Unreal, On Prajñā Being Non-knowing, On Nirvāṇa Being Nameless) plus the 'Essential Meaning of the Original' preface — synthesizes Nāgārjuna's Mādhyamika (via Kumārajīva's translations) with Chinese dialectical vocabulary and is cited throughout the Chan / Zen record (Nánquán, Huìnéng, Shítóu, Dàhuì).

dialogue.speaker: Sengzhao / 僧肇
dialogue.zh: 既無往返之微朕，有何物而可動乎？然則旋嵐偃嶽而常靜，江河兢注而不流，野馬飄鼓而不動，日月歷天而不周。復何怪哉？
dialogue.pinyin: Jì wú wǎngfǎn zhī wēi zhèn, yǒu hé wù ér kě dòng hū? Ránzé xuánlán yǎn yuè ér cháng jìng, jiānghé jīng zhù ér bù liú, yěmǎ piāogǔ ér bù dòng, rìyuè lì tiān ér bù zhōu. Fù hé guài zāi?

red_pine.text: Since there is not even a trace of coming or going, what thing can be in motion? Thus whirlwinds that topple mountains are eternally still, raging rivers rush to the sea yet do not flow, floating dust eddying in the wind does not move, and the sun and moon crossing the heavens do not revolve. Why should this seem strange?

cleary.text: If there is not even a hint of transit, what thing can move? So it is that violent winds uprooting mountains are perpetually calm, rivers racing onward do not flow, drifting dust does not stir, and the sun and moon traversing the sky do not turn. What is so odd about that?

liebenthal.text: There is no trace of things coming and going. What, then, is there that can move? Cyclones that level mountains are ever still; rivers rushing to the sea do not flow; the wild horse of blowing dust does not stir; sun and moon coursing the heavens do not circuit. Why be astonished?

dialogue.speaker: Sengzhao / 僧肇
dialogue.zh: 求向物於向，於向未甞無；責向物於今，於今未甞有。於今未嘗有，以明物不來；於向未甞無，故知物不去。
dialogue.pinyin: Qiú xiàng wù yú xiàng, yú xiàng wèi cháng wú; zé xiàng wù yú jīn, yú jīn wèi cháng yǒu. Yú jīn wèi cháng yǒu, yǐ míng wù bù lái; yú xiàng wèi cháng wú, gù zhī wù bù qù.

red_pine.text: If you seek past things in the past, in the past they were never absent; if you call past things to account in the present, in the present they are never found. Not being found in the present shows things do not come; never being absent in the past shows things do not depart.

cleary.text: Seeking past things in the past, in the past they were never nonexistent; holding past things to account in the present, in the present they never exist. That they never exist in the present makes it clear things do not come; that they were never absent in the past shows things do not go.

liebenthal.text: Seek past things in the past — they were never lacking there; tax past things in the present — they are never found here. Their absence in the present proves that they do not come; their presence in the past proves that they do not go.

sections.title_en: On the Emptiness of the Unreal

dialogue.speaker: Sengzhao / 僧肇
dialogue.zh: 夫至虛無生者，蓋是般若玄鑑之妙趣，有物之宗極者也。自非聖明特達，何能契神於有無之間哉？
dialogue.pinyin: Fú zhìxū wúshēng, gài shì bōrě xuánjiàn zhī miàoqù, yǒuwù zhī zōngjí zhě yě. Zì fēi shèngmíng tèdá, hé néng qìshén yú yǒuwú zhī jiān zāi?

red_pine.text: Now the ultimate void, unborn, is the mysterious object of prajñā's profound mirror, the ultimate pivot of all existents. Unless one is sagely, enlightened, and uniquely penetrating, how can one fuse spirit in the gap between being and non-being?

cleary.text: The supreme emptiness, free of birth, is the subtle direction of prajñā's mysterious mirror, the ultimate pole of all things. Apart from sagely brilliance and special attainment, how can one attune the spirit between existence and nonexistence?

liebenthal.text: Absolute emptiness, the unborn, is the wondrous theme on which prajñā reflects, the final norm of all beings. Who except the sage of extraordinary insight could unite with the spirit in the realm between being and non-being?

dialogue.speaker: Sengzhao / 僧肇
dialogue.zh: 天地與我同根，萬物與我一體。同我則非復有無，異我則乖於會通，所以不出不在，而道存乎其間矣。
dialogue.pinyin: Tiāndì yǔ wǒ tónggēn, wànwù yǔ wǒ yītǐ. Tóng wǒ zé fēi fù yǒuwú, yì wǒ zé guāi yú huìtōng, suǒyǐ bùchū bùzài, ér dào cún hū qíjiān yǐ.

red_pine.text: Heaven and earth share one root with me; the myriad things are one body with me. Those who are one with me transcend being and non-being; those who differ clash at every turn. Hence one neither departs nor abides, yet the Way dwells therein.

cleary.text: Heaven and earth have the same root as I; all things are one body with me. Identical to me, there is no longer being or non-being; different from me, communion is thwarted. Therefore neither emerging nor abiding, the Way exists within that interval.

liebenthal.text: Heaven and earth have the same root as myself; all things form one body with me. Whoever is at one with me is no longer concerned with being and non-being. Whoever differs misses the point of union. Therefore the sage neither comes forth nor abides within; truth exists in the space between.
